notes.22:
OPPORTUNITY SNAPSHOT
Abu Dhabi Police (ADP) is an existing Hub client, currently marked Opportunity. This is a new traffic-enforcement platform infrastructure opportunity. I found no linked project, contract, environment, or operational record for this work in the Hub.


CUSTOMER REQUIREMENT AND TECHNICAL GATE
On 8 October 2026, the customer requested pricing for servers, processing/GPU capacity, and operating licenses to start the work. Laith asked Dell for urgent hardware support and said the proposal was needed by 9 October for customer management review on Monday. The email thread includes a 12 October Dell call arrangement.


Following the customer meeting on 5 October, ADP reported on 6 October that the servers provided did not match the requested specifications and that required GPUs for the platform’s AI systems were unavailable. The customer requested corrective action and an expected completion date. This is a confirmed readiness blocker; I found no message confirming it was resolved.


COMMERCIAL OFFER SENT
On 9 October, Vitronic sent quotation RJ/VM/091026-01V01, dated 9 October, for datacenter hardware supply and installation. The attached three-page quote is in AED: subtotal AED 4,934,280, VAT AED 246,714.70, total AED 5,180,994. It lists three non-GPU Lenovo SR650 V4 servers, three GPU servers (each specified with two NVIDIA L40S GPUs), one high-availability server, two SAN switches, SAN storage, and a Veeam backup appliance sized for 90–100 VMs. Quoted availability for the server items is 8–12 weeks. Terms state 30 working days’ validity, delivery and installation, 20% advance, 70% on delivery, and 10% after installation and handover. These are quotation terms, not an executed contract or accepted order.


STATUS AND FOLLOW-UP
On 2 November, the latest email in the six-message infrastructure thread says Vitronic is still awaiting the customer’s response. I found no acceptance, purchase order, award, agreed completion date, or confirmation that the server/GPU readiness issue was fixed.
• Confirm whether ADP accepted quotation RJ/VM/091026-01V01 and whether its validity was extended or a revised quotation issued.
• Confirm technical compliance against the customer’s latest infrastructure requirements and closure of the GPU gap.
• Confirm delivery/installation dates and operating-license scope before creating an awarded project or contract.


SOURCE EVIDENCE
• “Abu Dhabi Police: IT Infrastructure & Integration Requirements” — six messages from 22 September to 2 November 2026, including the customer’s 6 October non-compliance notice, Vitronic’s 9 October quote submission, and 2 November follow-up.
• “Request for IT Infrastructure + GPU (Abu Dhabi Police)” — five messages, 8–12 October 2026.
• “ViTIP_AD_Quotation_Proposal_Datacenter_Solution.pdf” — three-page quotation RJ/VM/091026-01V01, visually reviewed.
• The 8 October supplier request references “BoQ_IT_Infrastructure_Requirements_ForSuppliers_V1.5.xlsx”; full line-by-line compliance remains to be checked.


PRIORITY: High — customer-reported infrastructure non-compliance and missing GPU capacity are unresolved in the latest reviewed correspondence, and the opportunity includes a material hardware quotation.
EVIDENCE STATUS: Confirmed customer report, quote sent, and 2 November response still pending. Award, accepted scope, resolution, and delivery commitments are unverified.


ATTACHMENT REVIEW — supplier BoQ (8 October 2026)
The attached workbook ‘BoQ_IT_Infrastructure_Requirements_ForSuppliers_V1.5.xlsx’ was opened in Outlook’s Excel preview. Its Infrastructure worksheet is titled ‘Vitronic Backoffice Server Requirements _ViTIP’ and lists VM requirements across three project phases, with fields for VM name, type, zone, product, operating system, mandatory status, and phase. The visible inventory includes Linux Ubuntu and Windows Server 2022 workloads.


The Resource Calculator worksheet assumes 300 ANPR devices and 100,000 captures per device per day (30 million captures/day). Its GPU workload table lists minimum GPU memory of 16 GB for ViLLC ANPR, Car Classification, and Make & Model, and 32 GB for Vision Connect and LLM ChatBot. A separate ViSM object-detection/tracking estimate uses 300 devices at 3 GB inference per stream. These are workbook sizing inputs, not proof of the final deployed capacity.


COMPLIANCE CHECK: The workbook provides useful sizing and OS inputs, while the 9 October offer quotes physical servers and GPUs. The reviewed material does not establish a completed VM-by-VM compliance mapping, GPU capacity validation against each workload, or confirmation that the customer’s supplied servers were corrected. Technical fit and acceptance remain open.
notes.23:
ISSUE SNAPSHOT
Abu Dhabi Police reported a security vulnerability affecting its systems. This note tracks the customer follow-up only; the technical details and affected component are not confirmed in the accessible email text.


HISTORY AND CURRENT STATUS
• 3 June 2026: ADP sent details supplied by its infrastructure and information-security teams in two JPEG attachments. Laith replied that the issue had been escalated internally and that the concerned team would provide feedback.
• 23 June: ADP said it was still waiting for a response because the issue was important to its work. The same day, an internal email noted ADP was following the issue regularly and asked whether the ICPO topic was resolved for communication with the GmbH project-management team.
• 8 October: ADP again said it was still waiting for a response regarding system updates.
No technical remediation, customer notification, test result, or closure confirmation appears in the reviewed thread. The two JPEG attachments (“الثغرة (1).jpeg” and “الثغرة (2).jpeg”) could not be read in Outlook’s preview, so severity, affected systems, and specific remediation are unverified.


FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED
• Identify the internal security owner and confirm the current investigation/remediation status.
• Review the original ADP evidence, assess affected systems and severity, and record the approved corrective action and validation result.
• Confirm whether ADP has been updated and whether the ICPO / GmbH project-management follow-up is still required.
No owner or due date is established by the reviewed messages.


SOURCE
“ثغرة امنية” — six-message Outlook thread from 3 June to 8 October 2026. Two JPEG attachments were present but not readable in Outlook preview.


PRIORITY: High for follow-up because the customer described a security vulnerability, reported operational urgency, and repeated the request after internal escalation. Technical severity remains unassessed; do not treat as resolved.

oyoonExistingNote.body:
OPPORTUNITY SNAPSHOT
Dubai Police / OYOON Center RFP 234: Zabeel virtualization cluster server expansion. The Hub has an existing OYOON relationship and active OYOON projects; this tender is tracked here as an opportunity, not as a new awarded project or contract.


CURRENT STAGE — TECHNICAL EVALUATION
On 20 September 2026, Vitronic requested confirmation of the technical evaluation so the financial evaluation could proceed. On 21 September, Dubai Police shared its evaluation of three bidders against the agreed vendor upgrade design and power/network requirements. No award, financial evaluation outcome, purchase order, or contract was found in the reviewed thread.


BIDDER EVALUATION REPORTED BY DUBAI POLICE
• Rank 1 — Alpha Data: 58/70, PASS. The evaluation says all 102 mandatory part numbers and quantities were exact; phase 1 is HPE dHCI expansion, with a phase 2 private-cloud option.
• Rank 2 — MDS Computers: 68/70, PASS. The evaluation says 100 of 102 mandatory part numbers were included; one Cisco part was substituted and not declared under TR15.
• Rank 3 — Computer Direct Access: 5.5/70, FAIL. The evaluation says zero of 102 mandatory part numbers were listed, quantities were absent, VMware licensing and PDUs were missing, and the offer validity was 30 days versus the required 90 days.
These are customer evaluation results, not confirmation of Vitronic’s selection or commercial outcome.


TECHNICAL / PROCUREMENT CONTEXT
The existing Zabeel environment was described as HPE dHCI hyperconverged infrastructure. Dubai Police advised that any expansion should retain compatibility with that platform. Vitronic raised concern in August that a Dell proposal needed final Dubai Police AI-team approval because the data center was originally built on HP. Later exchanges show the requirement moved toward HPE dHCI expansion and additional AI Agent resources, followed by a second tender round to obtain more offers.


FOLLOW-UP ITEMS TO VERIFY
• Confirm the final technical evaluation approval and whether the financial evaluation completed.
• Confirm the awarded bidder, procurement decision, and any purchase order or contract.
• Confirm whether Vitronic has a delivery or support role in the selected solution and whether the existing OYOON contract scope is affected.
• Confirm the final approved architecture, compatibility requirements, and the AI Agent resource impact.
No owner or due date for these follow-ups was established by the reviewed messages.


SOURCES REVIEWED
• “RFP OYOON 234 — Virtualization Cluster Server Expansion (Zabeel)” — thread through 21 September 2026 (13 messages).
• “OYOON 234 Zabeel servers expansion” — 25 June 2026 proposal thread. The attached technical proposal was not readable in Outlook’s preview; this note relies on the September evaluation table in the email thread.


Priority: Medium — active procurement with a technical gate and possible impact on an existing customer environment; award and Vitronic’s role remain unknown.

trafficExistingNote.title: MongoDB OpsManager OS upgrade – vendor VM readiness
trafficExistingNote.body: 09 Nov 2026 — The “OS Upgradation of MongoDB OpsManager” email thread is marked high importance. Mohammad Al Omari says another critical issue depends on resolution. Vendor Mathiyalagan said on 09 Nov that they will visit on 10 Nov to create two Ubuntu 22.04 LTS VMs. Earlier Hyper-V VM IP visibility and package/configuration setup issues were reported resolved on 12 Oct; the latest thread does not confirm VM creation, upgrade completion, or resolution of the dependent critical issue. Owner/team, affected service, and downstream impact are not specified in the reviewed thread. Follow up after the vendor visit to verify both VM readiness and the dependent issue, then identify the appropriate Hub team/client if further tracking is needed. Source: Outlook “OS Upgradation of MongoDB OpsManager”, Oct 12–Nov 09, 2026.

madarNotes.19:
PROJECT LINK
Hub project 113506-AE is now registered as Active under Madar Dijla. Owner is Laith Hamdan, based on the client profile’s Project Manager assignment. Service dates and supported products were left unassigned because the reviewed sources do not establish them.


PROJECT CONTEXT — 18 JUNE 2026 MEETING MINUTES
The six-page minutes cover the Iraq Ministry of Interior deployment for 100 enforcement bars. Madar had no usable customer-side environment, so infrastructure needed to be ordered and delivered. The plan discussed four HPE servers, physical hardware with virtualization (Nutanix or VMware options), high availability, database/application/DMZ zones, and a DR-side replication server. A full DR site was outside current scope. Storage sizing assumed three months of retention, with NAS to be considered afterward. The minutes warned delivery and integration could slip by up to an average of three months.


The minutes record eight follow-ups, with no action dates: Vitronic to resend the infrastructure master sheet/connection matrix and topology, confirm HA server resources, and share the latest BoQ; Madar to share the latest BoQ and formally communicate material changes from obsolete contract specifications to the Ministry; both parties to monitor delivery, align on delay risk, and define a workaround if the delay became unacceptable to the Ministry.


CONTRACT / SPECIFICATION CHANGE
The 30 June Arabic customs-exemption letter is dated 30 June 2026 (ref. VMME/ADMIN/0130/June26) and refers to Contract 2/2025 and Clause 6. Madar requested item-level shipment data for the Ministry submission, including item/serial details, net and gross weights, invoice/packing references, port, ETA, and supporting documents; follow-up correspondence also requested item and shipment prices. The Hub’s contract register showed no Madar contract during this review, so contract terms, dates, and current legal status remain unverified.


On 27 July, Madar said contracted infrastructure items were obsolete, end-of-life/end-of-support, or unavailable, and requested an HCI-based redesign. Vitronic requested an updated BoQ and quotation before comparing against contract scope and preparing formal Ministry approval. Laith later confirmed an official letter was attached. The reviewed thread does not confirm an approved revised BoQ, the adopted procurement path, or Ministry approval.


SHIPMENT ATTACHMENT REVIEW
The 29–30 June workbook lists Batch 01 with enforcement bars, quantity 10, 98 kg net / 132 kg gross, ETA 18 June 2026, port Trebil, and remark “Received.” Batch 04 lists 45 units, with five identified as spares; its remark says shipment would follow Madar senior-management approval. The Batch 04 figures show 2,339 kg net and 2,020.5 kg gross (gross below net), an apparent data inconsistency that requires confirmation. The 18 June minutes separately forecast 50 bars expected on 26 June; the reviewed sources do not reconcile these batch counts/dates or confirm the final delivery status.


MINISTRY DEMONSTRATION — 21 OCTOBER
Madar reported that the Ministry wanted an enforcement-bar demonstration using a temporary server. Vitronic requested server IP/specification, OS/version, remote access, EB IP, and bidirectional ping results, and asked if the agreed infrastructure document was ready. The attached sizing workbook is titled “Vitronic Backoffice Production Server Requirements”; it sets out a multizone, phased production design, including 1.1 TB DB targets and CPU/memory ranges, but is not evidence of the temporary server’s actual capacity. No demonstration outcome or deployment decision was found.


OPEN FOLLOW-UPS
• Confirm the current approved BoQ, HCI/contract variation decision, and Ministry approval path.
• Reconcile shipment batch quantities, dates, customs submission, powering kits, and delivery; validate Batch 04 net/gross weights.
• Confirm the current contract 2/2025 terms and ensure the Hub contract register is complete.
• Confirm whether the Ministry temporary-server demonstration occurred and the resulting rollout plan.
Owners/due dates after the June minutes were not verified.


SOURCES REVIEWED
• “113506 Project Meeting Minutes” — 18 June 2026, six-page attachment and eight action items.
• “113506: Urgent Required Shipment Details for Customs Exemption” — 29–30 June, shipment workbook and Arabic letter attachment.
• “Request to Update Server and Network Infrastructure Technical Specifications” — 27 July, six-message thread.
• “113506: EB Connectivity for Ministry Demonstration” — 21 October, temporary-server request and sizing workbook.

• VIDPP-PRO-DB1 — DB | 8–16 vCPU | 64 GB RAM | 350 GB disk (C 100 / D 250 / E 0 GB). Docker stack: Delta Lake, Apache Kafka, FastAPI, Apache Spark, Redis, PostgreSQL, Apache Airflow, OpenTelemetry and Zipkin. Purpose: data extraction, processing, transformation and ingestion.
• VISDB-PRO-BGETL — DB | 8–16 vCPU | 64 GB RAM | 200 GB disk (C 100 / D 100 / E 0 GB). Docker; API purpose.


CAPACITY AND STORAGE
• 16 VMs. Row-level base disk total: 7,850 GB (C 1,600 / D 5,250 / E 1,000 GB). Workbook total with margin: 10,467 GB.
• CPU minimum sums to 128. Workbook summary states maximum 288 and maximum with margin 384. Recalculation of all 16 row maxima gives 304, which is 16 higher than the workbook summary. The workbook does not state the margin formula, so the 384 figure cannot be reconciled to the row-level total without clarification.
• RAM totals reconcile: minimum 672 GB, maximum 832 GB, maximum with margin 1,109 GB.
• Separate storage estimate: 88 TB, RAID 5, described as “S3 or SAN,” for video, EB ANPR passages, violations, records, a three-month archive and infrastructure with margin. The platform is undecided in the workbook; this remains a design requirement in this note, not a VM or a confirmed storage deployment.


HUB IMPORT AND BOUNDARIES
• Environment: /environments/13, linked to Madar Dijla project 113506-AE. The environment and all 16 VM records were verified in the Hub’s asset list on 9 November 2026.
• VM lifecycle / project phase: Planned / Requested. No IP, actual deployment status, technical owner, host, location or hosting provider was supplied.
• The existing Sewar Tech ViTIP environment /environments/11 was left unchanged. Some proposed names overlap its asset list, including VIITS-PRO-RTSP1/2 and VIDPP-PRO-APP1; the workbook does not assign those rows to Sewar. The Madar records are separately scoped under project 113506-AE.
• No standalone storage asset was created: the workbook gives a platform-ambiguous 88 TB estimate, not an identified storage system or instance.


FOLLOW-UP CHECKS
1. Confirm the CPU sizing with the workbook owner: row maxima total 304, while the summary says 288; confirm the correct margin basis as well.
2. Confirm whether the 88 TB storage requirement is S3-compatible object storage or SAN, and validate capacity, RAID and three-month retention assumptions.
3. Confirm project/BoQ approval and any HCI or contract variation before treating the design as a committed build.
4. When available, add the approved hosting/location, technical owner, IP allocation and implementation/deployment evidence to the same Madar infrastructure topic.

multicomNote:
PROJECT SNAPSHOT
115307-AE — Tunisia Speed Enforcement System for MULTICOM. The Hub project is Active. Contract register entry CT-1004 is Active and references PI2026_134, but its end date and renewal date are not recorded. The attachment reviewed is a commercial invoice/proposal, not an executed contract; no contract dates or terms are inferred from it.


COMMERCIAL DOCUMENT — 26 JUNE 2026
“PI2026_134 Tunisia Tender Commercial proposal.pdf” is headed Commercial Invoice, dated 26 June 2026, and totals €374,713.60 (prices stated net, excluding VAT, withholding tax, customs and other duties). It lists four CCH systems (€181,713.60), ViTIP Lite modules IDS/SDB/ITS (€100,000), integration development and implementation (90 days), a three-year ViTIP Lite license, training, and three-year warranty/maintenance (€93,000). These are document terms, not proof of an executed agreement, final acceptance, invoicing, or collection.


MEETING MINUTES — 27 AND 28 OCTOBER
The five-page minutes cover Tunisia system configuration, ANPR, Back Office integration, acceptance, delivery, and customer documentation. The expected customer visit was around 23 November 2026; target shipment was December, preferably the first or second week. Some spare parts might not be available by the visit or even year-end.


Agreed/required system behavior includes: ANPR visibility for every passing vehicle in Control UI (cars and trucks); speed-violation and passage-prohibition cases/reports; ANPR passage data for Back Office; health monitoring; six-lane PS Enforcement; case encryption/signing and update keys; external or internal NTP; and the agreed Kurdistan/Kenya configuration references with requirements documented precisely. The 28 October Back Office minutes specify passage XML metadata, overview and plate images, wanted-vehicle functionality, and no TUFF record for every passage. Router and camera configuration are required; video evidence integration to PS Connect is not currently required.


OPEN DECISION / ACCEPTANCE RISK
The minutes say current configuration will use Carmen, with future VIDE adaptation planned, but the longer-term VITRONIC OCR versus Carmen decision remains a strategic escalation. The sale handover reportedly omitted VITRONIC OCR-engine work from the scope handed to delivery. Final operational acceptance depends on the agreed solution working and data reaching the Back Office; customer-side connectivity is the customer’s responsibility, while Vitronic must be technically capable of generating/transmitting agreed data. Acceptance criteria and responsibility boundaries must be documented to avoid an open-ended acceptance process. The minutes also call for Germany project management to track customer acceptance and customer invoicing so headquarters closure aligns with subsidiary cash flow.


CARMEN DONGLE PROCUREMENT — 27 OCTOBER TO 2 NOVEMBER
The 27–28 October minutes mark procurement of four Carmen dongles as in progress, with supplier pricing and lead time to be confirmed and invoice to the LLC; they assign Mustafa. On 27 October, the COO said the purchase was time-critical and questioned why GmbH excluded the dongle from its ANPR obligation; John Yalda noted the right to reduce the intercompany invoice because ANPR was in scope. On 29 October, the minutes follow-up said the LLC should order the dongle for administrative reasons and that a supplier quotation was still pending before a purchase order.


On 2 November, a request was sent for four one-core North Africa Carmen Freeflow licenses/dongles (Vitronic article 149788; supplier article 8523499900), with commercial offer and earliest delivery date requested. Procurement reported that neutral-design dongles may take up to six weeks; supplier-branded versions can be faster but would reveal the external supplier to the customer. The reviewed thread does not show supplier quotation, branding choice, purchase order, receipt, or final resolution of GmbH/LLC scope and intercompany invoicing.


OPEN ACTIONS FROM THE MINUTES
• Before delivery: basic router script; camera IP/time/stream configuration; FM1 external NTP; PS Enforcement version/configuration ID; ComPC image and PS Connect compatibility; spare ComPC compatibility.
• ASAP: coordinate Carmen integration requirements.
• Before FAT/customer visit: define and document customer acceptance criteria and responsibility boundaries; share the FAT draft for customer review/approval.
• Customer documents still open: user, installation, maintenance, Control UI and TUFF Viewer training manuals.
• Dongles: supplier quote, delivery lead time, procurement path/branding, and intercompany scope remain unverified.
The minutes mark written Back Office requirements, data formats, Kurdistan configuration documentation and the follow-up software meeting as closed. No evidence reviewed here confirms completion of the remaining actions.


CONTRACT CHECKUP / FOLLOW-UP
• Confirm CT-1004’s executed agreement, end date, renewal/notice terms, and whether PI2026_134 is the controlling commercial basis. The Hub has no registered end or renewal date.
• Confirm final customer acceptance criteria, responsible approvers, and invoicing milestone.
• Confirm dongle purchase/receipt and resolve the apparent GmbH ANPR-scope versus LLC procurement/invoice adjustment issue.
• Confirm readiness for the expected customer visit and December shipment; track any unavailable spares.
No owner or deadline is added beyond the names/targets explicitly recorded in the minutes.


SOURCES REVIEWED
• “PI2026_134 Tunisia Tender Commercial proposal.pdf” — one-page commercial invoice dated 26 June 2026.
• “Minutes of Meeting-2728102026.docx” — five-page minutes for 27 and 28 October 2026, plus the 28 October open-actions table.
• “Project 115307: Request for Purchase of four Carmen ANPR Dongles for Tunisia” and “Project 115307: Carmen Dongle Procurement” — 2 November 2026 procurement thread, with 27–29 October correspondence in the thread history.

I would like to inform you that our company was not awarded the tender, as three competing offers were evaluated more favorably than ours.

 

However, there may still be an opportunity for our company to be reconsidered if the three competing candidates have not submitted the required Vitronic Code Source Modification Certificate, issued or validated by Vitronic as the code owner.

 

If none of the competing candidates can provide the required certificate, our company may have an opportunity to re-enter the evaluation process, subject to the tender requirements and the client's final decision.

 

The main concern is the time required for this process. Each bidder's call, presentation, and subsequent rejection procedure is expected to take more than 10 days. Consequently, our company may not be contacted for approximately one and a half months. This could significantly delay the final confirmation, potentially postponing it until the beginning of next year.

 

I will continue to monitor the situation closely and keep you informed of any further developments.

 

Cordialment, Kind regards, Mit freundlichen Grüßen

 

Ousama DIDOUQEN

ITD

VI-MA: TEAM Software : Team Lead - Software

Dear Naveed,

 

Hope you are doing well.

We have reviewed the ViSDB Technical Specification and requires confirmation that your solution aligns with our existing SQL Server AlwaysOn Availability Group (AG) environment. SSAS databases cannot be part of an Availability Group, so SSAS must act as a client of the AG and maintain its own high availability.

Our proposed approach is as follows:

Dedicated SSAS servers: SSAS will be installed on dedicated servers, not on the AG replica nodes, to avoid memory and CPU contention with the database engine.
Connection via the AG listener only : SSAS data sources will connect to the AG listener only, using the MSOLEDBSQL provider with MultiSubnetFailover=True. If a failover happens, processing reconnects to the new primary without any change to SSAS.
Process from a readable secondary : Cube processing will read from a readable secondary replica (ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly with read-only routing), so processing does not load the primary. Please confirm whether your solution needs to write back to the source during processing, because write back would require the primary.
Staging and data warehouse in the AG : Staging and data warehouse databases will be placed in the AG, unless staging can be fully rebuilt from source. In that case we would prefer to keep staging outside the AG to reduce log traffic.
AG-aware ETL and processing jobs : ETL and processing jobs will be AG-aware and run only on the current primary after a failover.
High availability for SSAS : Either:

(a) Two SSAS query servers behind a load balancer with a separate processing server, or

(b) An SSAS failover cluster instance.

Please tell us which one your solution supports.

Please confirm that your solution works with this approach, or tell us where it does not.

In particular, we need you to confirm:

SSAS mode (Multidimensional or Tabular), edition and version
Expected cube size, processing frequency and processing duration
How the Analytical Service Layer authenticates to SSAS and applies role and jurisdiction security (Kerberos delegation, EffectiveUserName or CustomData)
Server sizing (CPU, memory, storage) for SSAS in both Test and Production
Any dependency on a specific node name or instance name instead of the listener
We will build Test first and validate a full AG failover during cube processing before going to Production.

 

Best Regards,

Waqas

rnpNote: 2026 YTD risk from the 25 May–26 Aug Outlook thread “REQUEST FOR BACKUP FIBER CONNECTIVITY” (9 messages). KTRN stated on 3 Jun that the backup fiber was installed, but activation and remaining project activities were on hold pending a go-ahead. On 2 Jun, VITRONIC indicated it had no objection to proceeding; KTRN’s 2 Jun reply said activation would involve interface configuration and routing, with technical preparations complete and no service impact expected from activation. On 26 Aug, Alain Manzi again requested an update and stated that without the backup link the data center lacks high availability, so any issue could cause a critical service outage affecting essential public services in Rwanda. Verified: link installed; activation status is not confirmed in this thread; latest follow-up requests an update. Inferred risk: single-link dependency may remain if backup activation is still pending. Priority: High due to potential impact on essential public services, subject to confirmation of current link status and actual redundancy. No Hub ticket or note matched “backup fiber”/“KTRN”; this is one distinct topic. Follow-up: confirm whether KTRN activated the backup link after the 3 Jun hold, test failover, and record evidence of high availability. Owner and due date are not established in the thread. Source: Outlook conversation “Fw: REQUEST FOR BACKUP FIBER CONNECTIVITY,” 25 May–26 Aug 2026, with KTRN and Rwanda National Police stakeholders. No external message sent.

2374 heading Mon 11/9/2026 1:21 PM, Value: 3, ID: MSG_AAIA9gndwAA_DATETIME
bodies:
Dear Stani, 




Following our morning call, we would like to highlight a challenge faced by Online Enforcement Bar Vehicle (EB) during operations to catch wanted vehicles uploaded into ComPc. 

With the current configuration, EB first checks its internal ComPC database before retrieving information from Tekana. This sequence creates a delay, as the vehicles may have already passed by the time EB's checks with Tekana. Consequently, RNP officers miss opportunities to identify and intercept wanted vehicles.




Proposed  Workaround : 

As a possible workaround, we proposed to upload the list of wanted vehicles directly into Tekana's Watchlist module. This would enable EB to automatically check and identify these vehicles through Tekana during roadside enforcement, just as it currently does when checking vehicles with outstanding traffic fines or expired/without motor vehicle inspection certificates.

However, the current Watchlist interface does not support bulk uploads through CSV or Excel file. We therefore request an enhancement to the module to allow the uploading of wanted vehicle lists in these formats.




Technical Assessment




@Laith Hamdan  on EB tablet endpoint, kindly advise whether implementing this solution would require additional development or whether the existing integration can accommodate it...




The complete list of wanted vehicles will be shared with @Stanley Mwizerwa in a separate email to give you an idea of the data format and structure required. 




Your feedback on the proposed solution and the required system enhancements will be highly appreciated.




Best regards,




NGIRABABO Jules

Project Manager Traffic Enforcement System

Tel Phone: +250 788 305971

E-mail: managertes@police.gov.rw

Dear Gaston,

 

The 18 hours per month are a fixed allocation, reduced from the 40 hours per month established in the previous agreement, as shown in the attached email. We made this reduction because the project required less involvement.

 

These hours cover meetings, planning, and coordination with our internal teams, Vitronic Australia, and the client directly. They are not an average calculated by dividing the total hours from September to September by 12.

takNotes.2:
POC STATUS
TAK Business Group (Ethiopia) – ViTIP Lite proof of concept and final certification readiness.


APPROVAL AND FUNDING CONDITIONS
On 22 October 2026, Abdullah Kair wrote that he would proceed with starting the POC, subject to his discussions with Laith, Ryane’s approval, and Finance accepting a €4,000 fee waiver funded from the Sales Department budget. The email records conditions for proceeding; it does not confirm that each approval or the waiver was completed.


INFRASTRUCTURE READINESS
On 28 October, Abdullah sent Tsega Solomon minimum IT requirements for setting up the POC and asked him to arrange the setup for a final certification requirement. The attached workbook, “Ethiopia_117314_VITIP.POC.IT.Requirements.V1.xlsx,” contains two worksheets. The visible Pro+Stg Requirement sheet is titled “ViTIP Backoffice Server Requirements,” says the requirements are for the project’s first year, and lists three Phase 1 VMs: VITIP-POC-APP, VITIP-POC-WEB, and VITIP-POC-DB. The workbook preview exposed only part of the columns; full sizing, network and address values were not verified.


OPEN FOLLOW-UPS
• Verify Laith/Ryane approval and Finance acceptance of the €4,000 waiver.
• Confirm the customer-side POC environment is provisioned against the full requirements workbook.
• Confirm what “final certification” refers to, its owner and target date, and the POC outcome.
• Confirm completion of TAK’s product/asset onboarding documentation; 29 September email says three requested documents were provided for INSA, Ethiopia, but completion status was not verified.
No POC completion, certification result, final funding approval, owner, or due date was confirmed.


SOURCES REVIEWED
• “POC APPROVAL” — 22 October 2026.
• “Infrastructure Requirements” — 28 October 2026, and attached two-sheet workbook.
• Existing TAK POC scope/requirements correspondence.

takNotes.21:
OPPORTUNITY SNAPSHOT
TAK Business Group, Ethiopia — potential toll-road traffic-enforcement and ViTIP Lite engagement. TAK is an existing client in the Hub. The reviewed mail supports an active proposal/qualification opportunity; it does not confirm an award, contract, or delivery project.


CUSTOMER NEED AND PROPOSAL DEVELOPMENT
In early September, TAK’s Michael Embaye said speed was the primary issue for its Toll Road project and requested a complete commercial proposal. The related exchange clarified that the proposed anti-vandalism feature was limited to the housing (anti-impact). TAK also raised a question about the quotation section on proposal page 8; Vitronic replied that the quotation was included and the document had been corrected.


On 28 September, Laith instructed colleagues to use the ViTIP Lite proposal version 1.0. On 1 October, Abdullah circulated “ViTIPLite_Ethiopia_V1_2.docx” for internal technical review before it was to be sent to TAK. The reviewed messages do not confirm that version 1.2 was sent or accepted. A 1 September response also noted that OEM certifications could not then be obtained; the remaining exceptions in that email were not fully verified in this review.


CURRENT STAGE AND COMMERCIAL CHECKS
Stage: proposal/qualification; current customer decision unknown. Priority: Medium, because the customer requested a complete commercial offer and Vitronic prepared a revised technical proposal, but there is no verified award or deadline.


FOLLOW-UPS TO VERIFY
• Confirm which technical proposal version and commercial quotation were actually submitted to TAK.
• Confirm whether the customer accepted the scope (including speed performance and anti-impact housing) and whether OEM certifications remain outstanding.
• Confirm tender/customer decision, commercial validity, budget, contract status, and any next milestone.
• Confirm whether this toll-road opportunity is linked to the separate ViTIP Lite POC/certification activity; the reviewed mail shows the same TAK/Ethiopia relationship but does not establish that the two are one engagement.
No project code, award, contract, owner, due date, or customer response after proposal preparation was confirmed.


SOURCES REVIEWED
• “Ethiopia (Request for Proposal & Documentation: PSOPLite & Traffic Enforcement Project)” — 31 August to 28 September, including the 31 August meeting and proposal/clarification messages.
• “Software Technical Proposal Review” — 1 October, internal review request with ViTIPLite_Ethiopia_V1_2.docx attached. The attachment preview could not be read in Outlook; its technical details are not summarized here.
